metadata.title: SOAR Authority SSPP
metadata.remarks: This SSPP defines authoritative decision boundaries for Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR). It ensures automation accelerates approved actions without assuming detection, response, or governance authority.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits Security Operations authority and workflow constraints and SHALL NOT redefine decision ownership.

system-characteristics.system-description: Defines who may approve, enable, suspend, constrain, or revoke automated security actions and under what conditions automation may operate.

system-implementation.remarks: SOAR is an execution accelerator, not a decision authority. Automation operates only within explicitly approved bounds and is always attributable to a human authority.

automation-authority-scope.description: Authority to approve the use of automation for specific response scenarios.
Authority to immediately suspend or disable automation when unsafe, incorrect, or violating constraints.
Authority to permanently revoke automation privileges or playbooks.

authority-requirements.statement: All automated actions SHALL be attributable to a specific, authorized human role.
Automation SHALL NOT be enabled by default or through implicit tool behavior.
Automation authority SHALL be revocable at any time without system dependency.

automation-constraints.statement: SOAR SHALL NOT independently determine maliciousness, incident status, or severity.
SOAR SHALL NOT perform forensic acquisition, analysis, or evidence modification.
SOAR SHALL NOT accept risk or close violations.

control-implementation.description: Controls ensure automation authority is explicit, attributable, and governed.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Automation authority and responsibilities are formally defined.
Automation supports incident handling only within approved procedures.
Automation authority is governed as part of security planning.

statements.statement: SOAR SHALL NOT be used to bypass detection validation, response authority, or governance escalation.
Automation SHALL fail closed when authority, preconditions, or evidence integrity is uncertain.
Human authority SHALL override automation under all circumstances.
Automation misuse SHALL be treated as a control violation under the Violation & Drift Escalation SSPP.

back-matter.remarks: All SOAR-related SSPPs and playbooks MUST reference this SSPP. No automation may operate outside boundaries established here.
